doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Waiting for the twenty-first century; closing reflections
summary: Allen jokes about still waiting for money, says Sun Ra's spirit lives on, and that devoting his life to him brought discipline and responsibility; thanks and goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: This has been really fascinating for me talking to you, and I want to thank you for your time and I want to read a quote to sort of wrap up. And you were writing about the time that you were getting to know Sun Ra and you wanted to get going and he kept talking about the Bible and Egyptian mythology and then he said, “We’re going to play this music for the twenty-first century.” And you said, “I’ve got to wait that long?”
Yeah. With no pay or half pay. No you mean I had to wait until the twenty-first century to make some money?
Well now you’re in the twenty-first century, you’ve been doing it for —
Still haven’t made no money. So I’m glad that the music, I’ve got the music, I put that out there.
All right.
I did something good. But the money ain’t come yet. Still waiting on it.
Where do you think Sun Ra’s spirit is now?

Well I know it’s around here. It has to be, because he had told us not to Harlem, Queens, [inaudible] over the thing, you keep moving. You know? You take the stuff he done that’s of worth and it’s for the people, and put that out there and you teach that and you carry on. You see?
Yeah. Well on that —
He did so many things that no one person can keep up with all of it. He was an unusual person. Never could find anybody like him in my life. And I just devoted my life to him you know, to his work.
And we’re glad you did, sir.
Well I am too.
All right.
Or else I’d be lost.
All right.
Going in another direction. Going on the right road going in the wrong direction.
Thank you, sir.
It’s worth it for me. It kept me with some discipline and some responsibility and all the things that I’ve been ducking all my life. Being responsible.
All right. Thank you very much.
You’re welcome.
